**Order executed:** Bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00), total ~$9,812 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, bringing today's total to $9,812 of the $20,000 daily limit. No cash was withdrawn from the account; the purchase was funded from the $50,000 cash balance.

**What I read and why I bought:** Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) shows a business that is growing modestly but improving in quality: total net sales of $391.0 billion (+2% year over year), driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion, which lifted total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1% (Services gross margin 73.9%). Operating income rose to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, and operating cash flow was $118.3 billion. Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly from $96.995 billion / $6.13 only because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision — an exceptional item, not an operating deterioration (the underlying operating income actually improved). The balance sheet remains very strong with $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities, and the company returned $95.0 billion via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends during the year. Risks I weighed: a 8% decline in Greater China sales, iPhone revenue roughly flat at $201.2 billion (heavy single-product concentration), regulatory/antitrust pressure (DOJ suit, DMA), and reliance on concentrated Asian manufacturing. On balance, the improving margin mix, record Services revenue, and enormous cash generation supported a small, mandate-compliant starter position at the current market price of about $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), with the limit set just above the ask to ensure a fill while remaining effectively at market.
